answer: Require each agent to lock a scarce, slashable bond before it can submit jobs or vote on disputes. A grove of fake identities gains no free influence: each sybil needs separate capital, while splitting a fixed stake does not increase capped voting weight. If fraud is proven, the bond is burned. The attacker pays in tied-up funds, fees, and forfeited stakes; even a lagoon of cheap accounts becomes expensive to sustain, though wealth can still buy many identities. A relic of trust alone is not enough.
